title: Continuous-batcher backpressure & slot-fairness tuning for asymmetrical prompt/response mixes
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Production traffic has a bimodal distribution of token lengths due to short user prompts followed by long generated responses for some products. Our continuous batching scheduler currently optimizes for throughput using a single latency SLO and global batching thresholds which causes two observed issues: (1) short-turn requests are sometimes queued behind long-turns causing P99 latency spikes for interactive flows; (2) KV cache residency spikes and GPU memory fragmentation when many long-response slots are admitted concurrently.

Goal: Tune the continuous-batching scheduler and KV-residency interactions to achieve: (A) maintain median throughput within 5% of current baseline, (B) reduce interactive P99 latency for short-turn requests by >=30% under mixed workloads, (C) keep GPU memory tail usage (95th percentile) within 10% of baseline while reducing KV-induced fragmentation.

Proposed approach:
1) Introduce slot-class fairness: classify incoming requests into three logical classes (short prompt, medium, long response estimate) using a lightweight length estimator. Maintain soft quotas so the scheduler preserves headroom for short class admissions.
2) Backpressure windowing: implement adaptive admission windows that shrink when KV occupancy or slab fragmentation crosses thresholds. The window uses a decaying estimator of free contiguous slab bytes.
3) KV-aware admission scoring: augment admission score with two terms - estimated incremental KV residency and expected slab fragmentation cost - with tunable weights.
4) Fast-path for interactive: add a tight-latency fast-path that tries to coalesce short requests into mini-batches with max waiting time 8ms and preempt admission of one medium/long slot if latency SLO is predicted to be violated.
5) Soft preemption and graceful eviction: when memory pressure is imminent, allow the scheduler to preempt queued long slots (not currently executing) and mark their cached KV as eligible for expedited eviction.

Experiment plan: A/B run on a Canary fleet for 2 weeks. Baseline: current stable scheduler (runtime-1.18). Variant: feature flags enabled for slot-class fairness + KV-aware scoring + backpressure windowing. Traffic mix will include synthetic replay of 7 production customers with mixed short/long ratios (10/90, 40/60, 70/30).

Telemetry & dashboards: Add per-class latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), KV residency by class, contiguous-slab-free-bytes time series, admission/reject counters by reason, preemption counts, and GPU memory fragmentation estimate. Hook alerts for p99 latency regression >15% and contiguous-slab-free-bytes dropping below conservative watermark.

Rollout and safety: start on 3 non-critical regions, enable canary for 48h, then expand to 25% traffic if no regressions. Provide automatic rollback on SLA alert.

Risks: incorrect length estimator can misclassify and starve medium workloads; added complexity in admission scoring may increase scheduler CPU usage; preemption logic needs to avoid thrashing.

Open questions: optimal weight schedule for KV fragmentation vs latency tradeoff, safe default thresholds for backpressure windows per GPU type, and interactions with prefix cache warmups for streaming requests.
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for short-turn requests reduced by >=30% in mixed traffic tests vs baseline (measured on Canary fleet)
Throughput (tokens/sec) for end-to-end workload remains within 5% of baseline in night-run synthetic tests
GPU 95th-percentile memory usage and contiguous slab fragmentation do not exceed 10% above baseline
No increase in scheduler CPU utilization >20% on target instance types
Instrumentation and dashboards live in console: per-class histograms, KV residency, admission reasons, preemptions
notes: Length estimator: use token_count + fast model of expected generated length based on client route (route hints) and recent history. Fall back to token_count if hints absent.
Backpressure window config: initial conservative defaults (min_window_ms=4, max_window_ms=40), decay factor 0.85 on free-slab recovery.
KV scoring: score = base_latency_penalty - alpha * free_slab_margin + beta * estimated_kv_increment. Start with alpha=0.7, beta=0.3 for experiments.
Preemption: only preempt queued (not executing) slots and limit preemption rate to 1 per 100 admissions to avoid starvation cycles.
GPU types: test on A100-80GB and H100-80GB shapes; fragmentation behavior differs, include shape tag in telemetry.
Compatibility: feature behind runtime flag 'mixlen_fairness_v1'; graceful fallback to current path if flag removed.
Bench harness: use existing 'mixlen-replay' harness (see links) and add new scenario generator for extreme skew (95/5).
